messages.subject: Controlling facet height with ggplot2
parts:
Dear group,

I'm trying to create a multivariate time-series plot with ggplot2,
where each time series appears on its own facet. This is very similar
to the plot of Figure 7.5 on p. 122 of the ggplot book.

HOWEVER, there is a problem: I want the "top" plot to be more
important, and therefore I want its facet to be taller. The other
plots are less important, and should be smaller. Moreover, all y
scales are widely different, and thus the "space" argument to
facet_grid does not really apply. Is there any way to DIRECTLY
control the facet height (and eventually width) in ggplot2? I
searched on this list and read all relevant entries in the "Learning
R" blog, and I didn't find any way to accomplish this.

Any help is greatly appreciated.

Many thanks!
+ Nicolas

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Controlling facet height with ggplot2
parts:
Hi Nicolas,

No, that's currently not possible, but you could use grid to layout
out two plots (with different widths) on the same page.

Hadley
